articles.title: 'You're Going to Take a Hit': Rainbow Six Siege Director Bracing for GTA 6 Launch Impact, Promises Players Who Stick Around Will Be Served 'Like Kings and Queens'
articles.summary: Ubisoft has discussed how it is bracing for the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, and plans to reward Rainbow Six Siege players who stick around "like kings and queens."
articles.body:
Ubisoft has discussed how it is bracing for the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 , and plans to reward Rainbow Six Siege players who stick around "like kings and queens."

Despite still being several months away, the impact of GTA 6's launch this November is already being felt throughout the video game industry, with other game publishers crowding their own releases into September and early October in order to steer well clear.

Currently, no other publisher (apart from Nintendo and its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake) seems ready to brave November with a big-budget launch of their own. But what about live-service games which have to keep going during the peak of GTA 6's interest? Well, it's expected that they will likely see their own numbers dip.

Rainbow Six Siege X: Dual Front Mode Screenshots

"We've got a massive launch coming with GTA," acknowledged Joshua Mills, creative director of Ubisoft's long-lived Rainbow Six Siege, in conversation with The Game Business . Launched back in 2015, it continues to be enjoyed by a dedicated audience today — though even Mills admits that he expects many of these players to dip out and try Rockstar's blockbuster when it finally arrives.

"It doesn’t matter what genre you're in – you're going to take a hit when that drops," Mills continued. "People are going to play it, and then they’ll come back. Heck, all of us are going to play it. It's about being smart with your expectations so you can keep the team and HQ aligned. If the team sees player numbers dip, they can get anxious, but it's generally temporary."

And for those who do stick around, it sounds like Ubisoft's team is planning one of the best times to play in years.

"Our golden rule is to serve the players who stay like kings and queens," Mills concluded. "We don't go on vacation just because a competitor is swelling the market. We double down and reward those spending their valuable time with us. Funnily enough, Season Four will drop right around that time. That shifts up the game in different ways. We actually have some unannounced surprises held back to make a splash."

It's an intriguing tactic: not deliberately ceding ground to GTA 6, even while acknowledging the inevitable interest in the game that will likely deflate Siege's own player numbers — temporarily, at least. I'll be interesting to see what other live-service games might do, too.

articles.title: How Best Buy Became a Hidden Haven for Authentic Pokémon TCG Drops at MSRP Prices With Anti-Scalper Queues
articles.summary: Looking for authentic Pokémon TCG cards? Best Buy offers a wide selection, MSRP pricing, and strong bot protection to beat the scalpers.
articles.body:
Editor's Note: This article is sponsored by Best Buy. If you buy through our links, IGN may earn an affiliate commission. Learn more .

Collecting Pokémon cards has been a favorite pastime for millions of people for decades at this point, but in recent years, getting your hands on new drops has gotten increasingly frustrating. They’re cleaned out by bots almost instantly, scalpers charge double the price, and third-party marketplaces are full of resealed or weighed packs.

When you think of Best Buy , you probably associate them with TVs, laptops, and electronics in general. But what’s gone under the radar is that they’ve become a fantastic option for buying Pokémon cards thanks to huge stock, MSRP pricing, anti-scalper protections, early access, and authenticity guarantees.

If you’re a devoted Pokémon card collector, you probably already know that most stores that carry them have pretty limited variety. You can get a few booster packs and maybe a couple other options, but that’s pretty much it.

Best Buy might surprise you with how huge its selection is, including from the latest expansions. From the Mega Evolution Pitch Black series that launched with 120 cards in July, there are sleeved booster packs , booster bundles , and Elite Trainer Boxes .

That’s just scratching the surface of what’s available. Best Buy also carries previous expansions as well as coveted Ultra-Premium Collections (like Mega Charizard X Ex ) and other collector’s items (like the Pokemon Center Tohoku Special Box ). There are pages upon pages of available packs and boxes.

Life is full of annoying things, but near the top of the list is getting excited about an upcoming drop, only to have bots steal everything out from under you. Seeing “sold out” under a new release seconds after it goes on sale is a special kind of soul-crushing. Best Buy combats this with invitations, digital queues, strict purchase limits, and surprise drops.

Particularly popular upcoming releases will allow you to request launch day access ahead of time by signing into your Best Buy account and clicking “Invite to Purchase” on the item page. Best Buy will then alert a set number of people that they’ve been selected and provide a secure link where they have 24 hours to complete their purchase.

If a drop doesn’t have invites beforehand, you can use the Best Buy app to enter a waiting room on launch day. Everyone is limited to one purchase, which prevents a bot from swooping in and buying everything at once. It doesn’t guarantee every person will get what they want or that no scalpers will get in, since that’s unfortunately impossible. However, it evens the playing field to give real humans a chance to check out safely.

There are also sudden surprise drops that will go unannounced until they’re already underway, giving you the chance to spontaneously grab new cards. You have to be quick on these drops though, so follow Best Buy’s social channels to see announcements and jump on them immediately.

If you follow the prices of packs and boxes closely, you might have noticed that some shops and retailers will jack up the price on a set that has a lot of buzz. They’ll refer to this as “dynamic pricing,” but we call it a “hype tax.” Best Buy has declared that they won’t do that, they always stick to MSRP. So if a box normally retails for $49.99, that’s how much they’ll charge for it.

Nobody is going to complain about not paying extra money. For major collectors, that can save you hundreds of dollars a year, so that’s an obvious benefit of the guarantee. But it also helps with peace of mind, knowing you’re not going to get an unwelcome surprise once a new set goes on sale.

My Best Buy Plus is a membership program that costs $29.99 per year that brings benefits like members-only prices on certain products, an extended return window, and free expedited shipping. But the most relevant benefit when it comes to Pokémon card collectors is exclusive early access to TCG pre-orders.

If you have a My Best Buy Plus account, you’ll be able to access pre-orders before the general public, which can make the difference in getting the item you want. This still isn’t a guarantee that you’ll be successful, since it’s based on things like the amount of stock available and the level of demand. But it can give you a leg up.

Considering the steep difference in price between MSRP and the resale market, getting in on one pre-order you would have otherwise missed could cover the cost of a yearly membership. Only you can know if a membership is right for you, but if you make proper use of its benefits, you can end up saving more than you spend.

Another reality of our increasingly digital world is the risk you take having valuable things shipped to your home. Have you ever waited for a shipment like it’s a gift on Christmas morning, then had it arrive with the box dented and contents inside scratched? Or even worse, have you gotten a notification that your package has been delivered, only to get home and find that someone stole it off your porch? If you haven’t, trust us: it really sucks.

Best Buy has a hybrid purchase system that can help, giving you the convenience of shopping online but the reliability of picking up in person. Waiting in the queue, checkout, and payment can all be handled on your phone or computer, then just select in-store pickup and the location you want to pick up from.

Your local store will hold your order for up to five days, so you’re assured that your item will stay safe and secure until you’re able to pick it up. Of course, this means you need a store close enough to be able to visit in person, but with more than 1,000 Best Buy stores across North America, most people should have access to one.

How to Guarantee You Get Factory Sealed Items

Shopping online with big retailers can sometimes be confusing about who is actually selling an item, since third-party sellers can get mixed into search results without being clearly labeled. That can mean you’re at risk of buying fake cards or resealed packs from a seller you don’t know.

Best Buy also has third-party sellers, so you still need to be vigilant and make sure you verify who you’re buying from, but that’s very easy to do. Just look above the “Add to Cart” button on the item page and make sure it says “Sold by Best Buy” instead of “Sold & shipped by [seller name].”

If you don’t even want to see items being sold by third-party sellers, you can easily do that too. When you filter your search results, simply click the “Store Pickup” option. Since it’s impossible for third-party sellers to allow in-store pickup, this ensures all listings you see are actually from Best Buy.

All items bought directly from Best Buy are guaranteed to be factory sealed straight from The Pokémon Company, so as long as you pay attention to what you’re buying, you can be 100% certain of their authenticity and condition.

All of these features combine to make Best Buy a worthy option for buying new Pokémon cards. There’s a huge selection to choose from, you know you won’t have to pay above MSRP, there are bot protections in place, membership options allow for early access, and it’s easy to ensure you’re getting authentic items.

So if you’re a long-time collector who’s sick of dealing with scalpers, you’ve been scammed into buying fake cards before, or you’re just looking for a place you know will have the next big drop, Best Buy should be your first stop.

articles.title: Minecraft Beat Itself After Nearly Two Billion Simulated Years
articles.summary: Minecraft is no stranger to simulations, but it turns out that under the right conditions, the game can beat itself if given billions of years.
articles.body:
Minecraft is no stranger to simulations, but it turns out that under the right conditions, the game can beat itself... if given billions of years.

This was discovered by YouTuber RedLogic , who built a custom Minecraft simulation to see if the game could ever beat itself without a player ever joining. Two billion years is a bit too long to watch this play out in real time, of course, so he used a Monte Carlo simulation to "compress billions of ticks into explicitly sampled waiting times, while explicitly tracking rare events and the physical resources that can advance or destroy the chain."

Minecraft Chaos Cubed Screenshots - Minecraft Live March 2026

But it wasn't just a case of time, either. RedLogic needed a Minecraft seed with the right amount of resources and a naturally-occuring ender portal, otherwise the game wouldn't be able to actually complete itself. So, of course, he ran another simulation to find the perfect world and then set the model loose.

While the game did eventually beat itself, it did so at a glacial pace, with tens of thousands or even million of years between milestones. The endermen didn't even find the portal to the dragon until 35,510 years into the simulation. From there, it was a process of waiting for endermen to find the entrance to the portal, enter it and build towards destroying the dragon's End Crystals.

But because these are NPCs with random behavior, the process took millions of years and relied on blocks happening to be dropped in the right place. After three million years, a snow golem shot a projectile at an enderman, and destroyed one of the End Crystals. From there it was just a question of repeating that event nine times, and then getting creepers to explode and damage the dragon enough to kill it. All told, the simulation took 1.97 billion years to complete, but it did complete.

Obviously it's much faster to go in and kill it yourself, but the fact that this was even possible is part of the reason Minecraft has endured as long as it has . And seventeen years later, it's proving that anything is possible. Players can even sit down now.

articles.title: MANHATTAN UNDER SIEGE
articles.body:
As Manhattan continues to experience supernatural unexplained incidents, IGN has been sent a video secretly leaked by an anonymous source at the FBC, the Federal Bureau of Control.

Kept hidden from the public for decades, the FBC’s main charter is to investigate so-called "paranatural phenomena." Knowledge of their existence only came to light when the formerly secret government department released a public information campaign on how to stay safe from paranatural forces.

The subject line of the leaked video’s accompanying email reads: “Ignore the FBC. We are doomed.” Shot on a mobile phone on Thomas Street, the footage appears to show a number of figures levitating and surrounded by a red light emanating from various skyscraper windows. Sources with former ties to the FBC claim these incidents are caused by the Hiss, a hostile paranatural entity that corrupts human minds and represents a significant threat to the entire population of NYC.

The video’s authenticity is further supported by witness statements who claim to have seen the phenomenon firsthand. Michael Bamber, 33, a clerical worker with the NYC Port Authority, said: “I was walking to the subway when red started appearing everywhere. But I didn’t just see red, I could hear it, smell it even. It was crazy.”

Another witness, Cherry Connor, 27, a deputy administrator for City Hall, said: “I was just leaving work when people started floating up into the air. They kept on making these strange sounds, like they were chanting something. Then the woman right next to me started making them. Her eyes rolled into the back of her head and then she just took off, right off the ground. Then I started running. Everyone around me was screaming. It was horrible.”

Sources close to the 911 switchboard reported a massive spike in emergency calls during the phenomenon’s appearance and local hospitals were flooded with people suffering from hysteria and injuries caused by the sudden stampede of onlookers from the area.

This event is the latest in a series of paranatural phenomena that has wreaked havoc on Manhattan. However, when asked for comment, the FBC completely denied the appearance of the Hiss and blamed the apparent sighting on a mass hallucination. An FBC press officer said: “Hallucinations are very common and we believe that the recent bout of mass hysteria that New Yorkers have experienced has caused a mass hallucination. The Hiss are not in fact in Manhattan. Remember - no matter what you see, just trust the FBC. Thank you.”

In response to the FBC’s comments, Mr Bamber, the eyewitness to the Thomas Street incident, said: “The FBC are talking out of their f**king ass. Mass hallucination?! Bullshit! I saw the whole thing. People need to wake up. This is f**king serious.”

If you have witnessed the Hiss or any of the strange phenomena in Manhattan, please contact IGN. We want to hear your story.
